mathematical_justification: All 11 parents were read: local/Tor/regularity criteria, fibre constructions, Henselian lifting, fibrewise maps, relative assassin, syntomic fibres and coefficient rings. They use A/m for the specified commutative local ring, including A=R_p and scheme local rings. For a proper maximal ideal m in a unital commutative A, a∉m gives (a)+m=A, so ra+b=1 for some b∈m; [r] inverts [a]. Thus A/m is a field, but a bare field definition does not specify its quotient construction, map or relation to (A,m). Generic quotient rings need not be fields, and Frac(D) preserves an embedded domain instead of killing a maximal ideal. For A=Z_(p), its residue field has characteristic p while Frac(A)=Q has characteristic zero, disproving a general residue/fraction-field identification. In coefficient-ring contexts an induced residue-field isomorphism is a map between such fields, not the residue field itself.
